title: Palindrome-Ready Subsequences
body:
You are given a string s of length n made of lowercase English letters. Count the subsequences of s whose letters can be rearranged into a palindrome. The empty subsequence counts as a palindrome.

Subsequences are counted by the positions chosen, so two equal strings taken from different positions are different subsequences. Return the count modulo 109 + 7.

Function to complete

Complete countPalindromicSubsequences(s). It returns the count modulo 109 + 7.

  • s: string of lowercase letters

Input reading and printing are handled for you, like on LeetCode. The input format below is what the tests and Custom input use.

JavaScript: products of two values below 109 + 7 overflow a double, so use BigInt for the modular arithmetic.
out: The value your function returns (the driver prints it): one integer: the count modulo 10<sup>9</sup> + 7.

samples.ex: The 8 subsequences by position are "", a, a, b, aa, ab, ab, aab. All except the two ab can be rearranged into a palindrome (aab → aba), so the answer is 6.
The empty subsequence and the three single letters. Any two or three distinct letters have more than one odd count.

ref:
class Solution:
    def countPalindromicSubsequences(self, s: str) -> int:
        MOD = 10**9 + 7
        cnt = [0] * 26
        for c in s: cnt[ord(c) - 97] += 1
        # a letter that appears c > 0 times can be taken an even (or odd) number of times in 2^(c-1) ways
        ev = [pow(2, c - 1, MOD) if c else 1 for c in cnt]
        od = [pow(2, c - 1, MOD) if c else 0 for c in cnt]
        pre = [1] * 27; suf = [1] * 27
        for i in range(26): pre[i+1] = pre[i] * ev[i] % MOD
        for i in range(25, -1, -1): suf[i] = suf[i+1] * ev[i] % MOD
        ans = pre[26]                    # every letter even
        for j in range(26):              # exactly letter j odd
            ans = (ans + od[j] * pre[j] % MOD * suf[j+1]) % MOD
        return ans
